title: Scoped microbatch interleaving with token ceilings to shrink reranker tail latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: The reranking endpoint sees high tail latency when a small fraction of requests have much longer token windows (long contexts or many candidates). These long requests occupy microbatch deadlines and cause short requests to wait, increasing P95/P99. Goal: reduce tail latency without harming rerank quality and without a material drop in overall throughput. Approach: introduce scoped microbatches with per-request token ceilings + interleaving scheduling that prioritizes short-token windows while allowing safe parallelization of long requests in opportunistic lanes. Add adaptive soft-timeouts (graceful partial scoring) and a lightweight fallback path that uses a distilled scorer when deadlines threaten to be missed.
acceptance_criteria: P95 latency for rerank under production mix reduced by >= 25% compared to baseline (measured on staging with x3 load).
Tail (P99) latency reduced by >= 30% on the NRT cluster during synthetic bursts with 15% long-context requests.
NDCG@10 regression <= 0.4% vs current scorer on evaluation set (quality preserved).
Throughput (req/s) difference <= 5% vs baseline in sustained load tests.
No increase in out-of-memory or misrouted KV-cache misses in 72h soak run.
design_notes: Scoped microbatch: each incoming request gets a token-ceiling hint computed from sequence-length histogram + candidate-size; the dispatcher groups requests into lanes: short, medium, long. Short lane is scheduled with strict microbatch deadlines and preemption-friendly I/O. Long lane uses opportunistic parallel workers that pull KV cache asynchronously and yield when short lane deadlines approach.

Interleaving: implement cooperative yielding inside the serving runtime loop (checkpoints per chunk) so long requests can be paused to let a short microbatch run; avoids hard preemption overheads of OS thread kills.
Token ceilings: enforce soft token ceilings per request (e.g., 64/256/1024 buckets) with optional token-shedding strategies (trim candidate sequences using cheap lexical filter before model scoring).

Adaptive soft-timeouts: per-request deadline calculated from SLA + current queue depth; if soft-timeout hits, run distilled scorer on remaining candidates and attach metadata about early-exit to response for downstream de-dupe.
KV cache policy: add a transient prefetch window for long-lane requests with lower priority; enforce capped concurrent KV fetches and LRU-with-deadline eviction to avoid cache thrashing.
Fallback model: distilled 50% smaller reranker selected when deadline breach likelihood > 0.6; must be validated vs primary for quality delta.
Instrumentation: add per-request lane tag, token_ceiling, soft_timeout_reason, fallback_used flags to traces and metrics.
implementation_tasks: Dispatcher: extend request metadata to include token_ceiling and lane_hint (ENG change).
Runtime: implement cooperative checkpoint/yield API and integrate with existing microbatch loop.
Scheduler: lane-aware packer that prefers high density short-lane batches; maintain separate queue depth counters per lane.
KV cache: add priority tiering to cache fetcher; metric emits on fetch latency by lane.
Fallback path: wire distilled model variant selector and plumbing to response schema (structured output field fallback_info).
Config: feature flag (rerank.interleaving.enabled) with traffic split control in console for canary rollouts.
E2E tests: unit + integration harness simulating mixed-length traffic, and synthetic soak tests for 72h.
Docs: update dev docs on batching semantics and new response metadata keys.
test_plan: Unit tests for dispatcher metadata propagation and checkpoint interrupts.
Microbench harness: replay production trace to compare baseline vs interleaved scheduler at x1/x3/x5 load.
Soak test: 72-hour run on staging with mixed request lengths, monitor P50/P95/P99 and memory/kv miss rates.
Quality evals: run NDCG, MRR on standard rerank eval set against distilled fallback and primary model.
Chaos test: simulate delayed KV backend and ensure short-lane unaffected beyond target SLOs.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated rollout: enable for 5% traffic in canary namespace (no SLA customers) for 48h.
If canary stable, increase to 25% over 24h, monitor P99 and fallback usage.
Gradual ramp to 60% with automated rollback if P99 increases > 10% vs baseline or fallback usage > 20%.
Full rollout to 100% after 7 days of stability signals and sign-off from SRE and ML QAs.
metrics: fallback_rate (percent of requests hitting distilled scorer)
risks: Quality regression from distilled fallback larger than expected — mitigate with AB tests and conservative thresholding.
Cooperative yielding complexity could introduce subtle deadlocks — add invariants and watchdog timers.
Cache eviction mis-tuning may increase KV misses for short requests — keep aggressive telemetry and revert knobs.
Rollback complexity if run-time changes interact with other experiments — coordinate with Platform experiments calendar.
